sections.h2: What sets Evans County apart on the Georgia map?
sections.html:
Of the four counties in the Census table, Evans has the fewest residents, 11,028 in July 2025, and the least land, 183 square miles. Its ground is coastal plain, the Canoochee River drains it, and Statesboro's micropolitan area absorbed it in 2023. Claxton holds the courthouse and the most people, while Bellville, Daisy and Hagan round out the four cities (Wikipedia).

The QuickFacts table shows 2.3 percent growth since 2020. Owned homes are worth $138,200 at the median, rent is $719, and the typical household brings in $53,259. Owners occupy about two of every three homes, and the county issued just 25 building permits in 2025.

sections.h2: What is the story behind Evans County's creation?
sections.html:
Voters ratified a constitutional amendment on November 3, 1914, that carved Evans out of Bulloch and Tattnall counties. Supporters wanted a nearer courthouse, more office jobs and more hotels and eating places, and some thought a minority in Reidsville controlled Tattnall. The Savannah and Western Railroad created stations that grew into Bellville, Claxton, Daisy and Hagan.

The current neoclassical courthouse in Claxton was finished in 1923. In July 1940 the federal government bought land for Camp Stewart, later Fort Stewart, and an estimated 1,500 people were displaced across the counties involved. Evans Memorial Hospital opened in December 1967, and the Evans County Heart Study ran from 1958 to 1995.

Wikipedia names Claxton Poultry Company, Valmont Newmark, the Georgia Department of Corrections, Camellia Health and Rehabilitation and Pinewood Christian Academy among the larger employers.

sections.h2: Where are the Evans County tax offices?
sections.html:
The commissioner's counter is in Claxton, and the assessor answers on the same county line. Street address and hours come from the commissioner's department page.

  • Tax Commissioner: Suite 4 at 201 Freeman Street in Claxton, or by mail at P.O. Box 685; call 912-739-1147 between 8:15 and 4:30 on weekdays.
  • Main county line: 912-739-1141, where option 1 reaches both tax offices; the contact page shows a lunch closing from noon to 1.
  • Records: parcel and exemption information appears on the assessor's qPublic pages.

With a small staff, the office would rather receive faxed or emailed paperwork and send answers back, though visitors may still look through records at the counter. Start a payoff request early, because the phones stay busy around the deadline.

sections.h2: What does Evans County charge when taxes are late?
sections.html:
Evans keeps its late-fee schedule short. The deadline is December 20. Every month after it adds 1 percent in interest, and a flat 10 percent penalty arrives with day 91.

Evans County property tax FAQ: due date, late charges and lien
StepWhat the county says
Due dateDecember 20 each year
Interest1 percent added every month after the due date
PenaltyOne-time 10 percent after 90 days
Lien (fi. fa.)Filed on the Execution Docket with the court clerk once taxes are past due

A fi. fa. can follow your credit for as long as seven years, the county cautions. Its escrow position is also spelled out: the bill is addressed to the owner, since the commissioner cannot tell who holds the mortgage or whether an escrow account pays the tax. Mortgage companies ask for the figures every year.

sections.h2: How do Evans County assessments and appeals run?
sections.html:
Values come from the Board of Tax Assessors. A changed value comes with a notice, and the owner has 45 days from that notice to object. If the board holds firm, the assessor's page says the file moves on its own to the County Board of Equalization, which schedules a hearing.

An arbitrator can stand in for that hearing, and superior court sits above both. Only three arguments are accepted:

  • Whether the property is taxable at all.
  • The value placed on it.
  • Whether that value is uniform with similar properties.

Grumbling about the size of the bill does not count, since the bill flows from the millage rate. State guidance wants the appeal postmarked inside the window, so mail it early. Taxable value is 40 percent of market value.

sections.h2: Which exemptions and land programs does Evans County list?
sections.html:
Homestead applications are handled at the commissioner's office between January 1 and April 1, and an approved exemption carries forward each year. Ownership and residence on January 1 are required. File again if the deed changes hands, if a name is corrected on the deed, or if you move up to another type.

The assessor's page, which still carries older income figures, describes a standard $2,000 reduction, a $4,000 reduction for those 65 and up who pass an income test, a school-tax reduction of up to $10,000 starting at age 62, and $50,000 for qualifying disabled veterans and certain surviving spouses. Ask the assessors what the income limits are now. A deferral program also exists for low-income seniors, and the deferred amount is due when the home changes owners.

Farmland and timber follow separate rules. A Conservation Use filing must reach the assessors by April 1 with a $10 fee, and it commits the land to a qualifying use for ten years. Breaking the covenant can cost double the taxes saved. The deadline for freeport inventory filings is the same April 1.

sections.h2: What should an Evans County seller do before closing?
sections.html:
Get the commissioner's payoff on paper before the closing table. Older years are cleared first, and the sale contract settles who bears the current bill.

  • Clear any fi. fa. before the title search turns it up.
  • Once the deed is recorded, give the commissioner the buyer's mailing address.
  • With an escrow account, notify your lender after payoff.
  • Hold on to your warranty deed copy, and know that the court clerk can supply recorded ones.

Acreage adds one more step. The assessor's page says a buyer who keeps the original use of Conservation Use land can sign the covenant and avoid a penalty, but a change of use inside the ten years triggers all of them.

sections.h2: Why might an Evans County seller choose a cash buyer?
sections.html:
Someone paying cash and accepting the house as is does not argue over repairs, which helps when a tax bill or lien already sits on the parcel. Census shows retail sales of $21,195 per resident in 2022, the top figure of the four counties, alongside a 22.6 percent poverty rate and a 13.4 percent Hispanic or Latino population.

Speed and condition drive the choice. Either way, the commissioner's payoff comes first.

faqs.q: When does Evans County expect payment of the annual bill?
faqs.a: The date is December 20, according to the county's property tax FAQ. Interest of 1 percent accrues monthly afterward, and the one-time 10 percent penalty comes after 90 days.

faqs.q: Does the Evans County Tax Commissioner mail my bill to the lender?
faqs.a: No. It goes to the owner, since the office has no record of lienholders or escrow arrangements. Lenders ask the office for amounts each year.

faqs.q: What is the window to contest an Evans County value?
faqs.a: Forty-five days from the notice date. File with the Board of Tax Assessors, and an unchanged case moves to the Board of Equalization unless you elect arbitration.

faqs.q: What does a fi. fa. mean on an Evans County parcel?
faqs.a: It is a lien the commissioner records with the court clerk when taxes run past due. The county says it can weigh on your credit for up to seven years, so settle it before selling.

faqs.q: Where do Evans County homeowners file for homestead?
faqs.a: At the commissioner's office in Claxton, from January 1 to April 1. Dial 912-739-1141 and press option 1 for questions. An approved exemption renews itself until ownership changes.
